ai.description: Cantor's Pit Viper reaches 100 cm. It is bright green with a distinct white or yellow ventrolateral stripe and a reddish-brown tail. It features a triangular head and a prominent white postocular line.
ai.identificationRemarks: Cantor’s Pit Viper is best identified by its distinct, vivid yellow or white postocular stripe that extends clearly onto the neck, contrasting with its dark, mottled body.
ai.habitat: Cantor's Pit Viper inhabits the dense, humid tropical rainforests of the Nicobar Islands, typically found in low-to-mid-elevation forest undergrowth and canopy.
ai.behavior: Cantor's Pit Viper is primarily nocturnal, remaining camouflaged among foliage to ambush small vertebrates that pass within its striking range.
ai.reproductionNotes: Cantor's Pit Viper is ovoviviparous, typically producing litters of 6–10 young. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with births observed around August or September.
ai.distributionRemarks: Cantor's Pit Viper is endemic to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, where it inhabits tropical forests from sea level to moderate elevations.
